analysis.title: Hawks Squawk, Doves Dote, Dario In, Jensen Out: Bonds Jump As Stocks Dump Most Since Liberation Day
key_insights: S&P fell seven straight days, its longest losing streak since Feb 2020, and dropped over 7% to near 7,000 in its worst week since Liberation Day. NDX fell over 10% and closed over 17% below its high. SPX broke its 200-day for the first time since April.

Anthropic priced a record $107.3B IPO at $83, including a $26B placement with suppliers, at about a $1.5T fully diluted valuation. It opened at $111.50, hit $115.10, then fell to $83.10 on Friday after the greenshoe was fully exercised (147M shares at $83). The deal drained liquidity from gold, bitcoin, copper and chips.

Anthropic bull case is mechanical: book was 6-7x covered, Nasdaq 100 inclusion on Dec 21 with about $19B passive demand, and listed options start Monday. JPM's Adler: 'If everyone wants a clearing event, one might happen. If everyone needs one, it won't.'

Nvidia beat for the 17th straight quarter with a Q4 guide of $130B vs $125B expected and FY28 growth raised to 75% from 70%. The board shut the door on Huang's return and CFO Kress said Nvidia will be more selective on customer financing. The stock fell about 20% on the week, its worst since Oct 2008, with a 7th straight losing week and a new SEC accounting probe.

Nvidia's dialing back of the 'bank of AI' role is positive for NVDA credit spreads but negative for neoclouds that rely on residual guarantees. Of $545B of project finance, $320B needs a guarantor who has stepped back. McElligott says the NVDA backstop flipped from a long put to a short put for the market.

Positioning was already very light. Goldman Prime L/S net leverage fell 7.6 points this month to the lowest in over five years. HF tech weight is about 18% vs 29% index weight. Tech selling was the fastest in a decade (-4.4 z-score). Single stocks saw the largest weekly shorting since Jun '22.

Record dealer short gamma into OpEx amplified the selloff. S&P futures top-of-book depth was $4.2M on Wednesday. VIX briefly topped 40 and spot traded over 12 vols above UX1, the most inverted since April 2025. VIX closed above 32, the highest close since Liberation Day.

Fed stayed hawkish. Waller wants to 'shock people' and the October minutes show 'almost all' members see more hikes. Goldman sees hikes in December and March to a 4.25-4.50% peak. Weak data (Empire 7.8, Philly Fed 6.3 vs 20.1 expected, permits -7.4%) took the 50bp December hike off the table and January hike odds fell below 60%.

Treasuries rallied five straight days. The 10Y fell from 5.17% to 4.90%, ending its longest run above 5% since 2007, and the 2Y fell over 20bps. UMich 1-year inflation expectations dropped from 4.7% to 3.7%. Privorotsky likes receiving rates and owning duration and compares the setup to Nov/Dec 2018.

Credit weakened. IG spreads widened about 10bps to the widest since May 2025, with 7 of the 10 widest IG names AI-related. HY hit the widest since April and CCCs are above 1100bps. Goldman's 2027 outlook counts $985B of AI debt coming and urges reloading systemic hedges.

Commodities and metals were liquidated. WTI fell below $85 for the first time since August despite Hormuz attacks, as the IEA sees a surplus and Goldman warns of a 2M bpd glut in 2027. Silver fell 15% and copper and gold about 10%, with gold below $3,600 for the first time since Sept 2025.

The dollar hit its strongest since April 2025 and BRL had its worst week since Nov 2024. Bitcoin fell below $60,000 to its lowest since Sept 2024, seven weeks down in a row, erasing its post-August rally.

Equity funds still drew $59.2B globally (ninth straight week of inflows, most since mid-June) and US equity funds $45.7B, while money market funds and bond funds saw outflows. Retail and long-only buyers bought the AI dip while hedge funds sold.

Outlook: next week brings OpEx gamma reset, October PCE on Wednesday, November CPI, and the Dec 9 FOMC. Nvidia's board has about until Nov 25 to name a CEO. Author says bonds are right and the Fed will follow after November CPI, and advises selling rallies despite light positioning that could allow a sharp post-OpEx bounce.

market_movers.rationale: Beat and raise but fell about 20% on the week on Huang's no-return decision, reduced customer financing and SEC probes. Lowest since May 2025 and now below GOOGL, MSFT and AAPL in market cap.

IPO at $83 round-tripped from a $115.10 high to $83.10 as the greenshoe was exercised and no stabilizing short remains. Watch whether $83 holds, options start Monday and Nasdaq 100 inclusion comes Dec 21.
Tumbled Friday on an agentic AI threat to Credit Karma.

sector_views.rationale: Tech was the worst sector, with NDX down over 10% and neoclouds down over 20%. Positioning is extremely light, which leaves squeeze risk.
Strong dollar, high real rates and liquidation pressured gold, silver and copper. Central banks remain buyers.
Privorotsky favors receiving rates and owning duration as the bond market prices a slowdown.

earnings_insights: Nvidia Q3 FY27 reported 11/17 after the close: beat every sellside estimate for the 17th straight quarter. Q4 guide $130B (14-week quarter) vs $125B consensus expected, with zero China data center compute in the numbers. FY28 growth outlook raised to 75% from 70%.
Goldman's AI semis basket trades at 11x 2028 earnings vs 16x for the S&P.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Fell from 5.17% as haven and growth-scare bid beat the hawkish Fed.
Plunge supports the view the Fed is fighting the last war. Long-run expectations eased to 3.3%.
Strong consumer data, but offset by weak surveys and industrial output.
Goldman still sees hikes while the market has dropped the 50bp December hike.
First time below $85 since August despite Hormuz attacks, on surplus signals.
First break since Sept 2025 amid strong dollar and liquidation.
Shock that boosted global bond rally.

crypto_views: Bitcoin fell below $60,000 to its lowest since Sept 2024, down seven weeks in a row, after a Sunday liquidation cascade, erasing its post-August debasement rally.
Bloomberg equity analysts called bitcoin's pre-IPO slide statistically unusual and consistent with cash raising ahead of the offerings.
Glassnode noted coins bought in the past six months are now underwater.

trade_ideas.description: Receive rates and own duration, plus long front-end bonds alongside equity
trade_ideas.rationale: Bond market is starting to price a policy mistake and a transition from inflation to growth and liquidity problem.
trade_ideas.risk: Fed continues hawkish tightening and November CPI re-accelerates.

trade_ideas.description: Sell rallies in equities until the Fed pivots
trade_ideas.rationale: Fed has not acknowledged the slowdown and 'the market pivots when central banks pivot'.
trade_ideas.risk: Light positioning could produce a sharp post-OpEx squeeze.

risk_factors: Fed overtightening, with the Dec 9 FOMC and hawkish officials still discussing 50bp hikes.
Nvidia leadership vacuum, SEC and California probes, and reduced AI financing spreading to long-dated projects.
Equity supply, with about $120B raised in one week and SpaceX bonds at above 8% yields.
Thin liquidity and Thanksgiving-shortened week, with record short gamma rolling off.
AI-related credit stress, with $985B of AI debt coming.
China chip export curbs freezing investment decisions.
vol_and_positioning: VIX briefly above 40 and closed above 32, the highest close since Liberation Day. Spot VIX traded over 12 vols above UX1, the most inverted since April 2025.
Dealers ran record short gamma into Friday OpEx (SpotGamma). Goldman says dealers are right around max short vega into expiry, and Nomura CTA buy triggers sit about 2% and 4% higher.
Goldman Prime fundamental L/S net leverage is at a five-year-plus low, below Liberation Day lows. HF tech net weight is about 18% vs 29% index weight.

Goldman Coppersmith and Privorotsky see squeeze potential, with Privorotsky calling a tactical local low possible. Goldman notes when VIX starts mid-November above 18 it ended the year lower 14 of 17 times.
Goldman advises using year-end strength to reload systemic hedges in credit.
geopolitical: New US China chip export rules took effect Thursday, pressuring China's access to advanced chips, remote compute and manufacturing, and banks paused a $480M ByteDance chip loan.
Iran struck a US radar installation in Bahrain, tankers were set ablaze in Hormuz and the US struck IRGC sites on Qeshm Island. Houthis hit the Saudi PIF's headquarters. Crude still fell.
Trump-Xi-Putin summit in Shenzhen issued a declaration pledging to increase refined petroleum product supply.
Trump is reportedly weighing another Iran strike campaign but says 'we'll see what happens after New Year'.
Bessent reportedly gave Nvidia's board about 10 days to name a new leader and Huang is due to testify before House panels.

tension_points.bull_case: Positioning is the lightest in five years, flows show buyers waiting and Goldman says it may take little positive news to spark a squeeze.
tension_points.bear_case: An underweight crowd chases strength but doesn't buy dips, Fed remains hawkish and the Anthropic supply overhang persists. Author advises selling rallies.
tension_points.what_invalidates: If stocks can't rally with every systematic buyer primed, McElligott says it's not a positioning problem.

tension_points.bear_case: Greenshoe exercised in full leaves no stabilizing short, and nearly half of record retail volume was selling.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A break below the $83 offer price.
